verdict: All 16 numbered acceptance criteria pass, verified by execution rather than reading: node --check is clean on both files; transport.bridge.js exports exactly NULL_BRIDGE/bridge/bridgeReady/esc/fmtNum; bridge() duck-types signedIn inside try/catch and rejects a half-built {gems} object; the NULL_BRIDGE key set diffs to ZERO against window.MythicTransportBridge (index.html:207827-208054) — 36 keys on each side plus _null; all seven mutators return false; importing under a stubbed DOM registers window.MythicTransport + __mtr, injects #mt-css exactly once across two open() calls, warns exactly once, opens to a drawn panel with no bridge, and close() removes the node; the globals-trap grep returns only comments and bridge property names; no .from(/.rpc(; no discord/webhook/upload. As writing it beats the bar file (community.bridge.js) decisively — real rejected designs, declared authorities, and refusal semantics argued from measured incidents. What stops it winning is not a criterion but an integration defect the sibling file explicitly assigned to it: index.js registers rigs without rarity, condition or runsCap, so every rig lands on the server's runs_cap default of 3 while the fleet panel prints up to 10. The rig rarity ladder — the entire reason a Cinder rig is worth buying — is inert in play, and the panel advertises a number transport_dispatch() will refuse.
biggest_gap: index.js calls registerRig() without rarity, condition or runsCap at BOTH call sites (index.js:490 seedStarter, index.js:636 the 'register' action), so transport_rigs.rarity/condition are left unset and runs_cap falls to sql/038's `not null default 3`. contracts.js:840-861 names this exact hole and assigns the fix to the caller: 'runs_cap IS THE CALLER'S TO SUPPLY, AND THIS FILE WILL NOT DERIVE IT... a Mythic rig would run three times a day instead of ten... the fix is for the caller to pass it'. index.js has the data in hand — index.html's _transportGrantStarterRig() parks the vehicle with rarity and condition:'Clean' (index.html:80489-80500), b.lot() hands both back, and effectiveRuns() is already imported and already used in fleetBlock() — yet fleetBlock() computes runs client-side from the ladder while the row it renders was registered at 3. Fix: pass { rarity: veh.rarity, condition: veh.condition, runsCap: effectiveRuns(def.id, veh.condition, garageTier) } at both sites. Second, smaller instance of the same class: the 'repair' action sends the view row's vehicleId, but contracts.js repair() forwards it as p_rig_id and sql/038's transport_repair(p_rig_id uuid) looks up transport_rigs.id — a PP vehicle id is not that uuid, so the repair button cannot succeed.

THE GAP — sql/038_transport_companies.sql:276 'runs_cap int not null default 3 check (runs_cap between 1 and 10)'; contracts.js:881 'const cap = Math.floor(Number(opts.runsCap != null ? opts.runsCap : opts.runs_cap)); if (Number.isFinite(cap) && cap > 0) row.runs_cap = ...' — index.js:490 passes '{ free: true, starter: true }' and index.js:636 passes '{ free: false }', so cap is NaN and nothing is sent, while index.js:281-283 renders 'const base = num(call(effectiveRuns, 0, (def && def.id) || null, condition, garage.tier)); const runs = base + (base > 0 ? garage.runBonus : 0);'.
